newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Big Russian banker becomes head of media group.
newsitem.headline: Big Russian banker becomes head of media group.

text.p: Vladimir Gusinsky has resigned as president of one of Russia's biggest banks, Most Bank, to take over as chief executive of the Most group's media interests, ZAO Media-Most said on Monday.

Media-Most incorporates the Most group's stakes in Russia's independent television channel NTV, the new NTV-Plus satellite television venture, the Ekho Moskvy radio station, and the Sem Dnei publishing house, which issues the Segodnya and Sem Dnei newspapers and Itogi magazine, it said in a statement.
Gusinsky is one of a group of millionaire bankers and media powerbrokers, who supported President Boris Yeltsin in last year's elections.
At the end of December 1994 Gusinsky fled to London for several months after being openly threatened by Yeltsin's powerful chief bodyguard Alexander Korzhakov, who was dropped last summer.

Gusinsky's decision to move is part of a drive to draw a greater distinction between the Most group's media interests and its other operations in areas such as retailing and real estate, the statement said.
Boris Khait, president of the Most group's Spasskiye Vorota insurance company, will temporarily replace Gusinsky as Most Bank president.
Stakes in media have recently became increasingly popular among banks and big companies.
Several banks have taken a large minority stake in ORT public television.

The industrial group around one of them, Bank Menatep, has bid for a controlling share in the Literaturnaya Gazeta weekly and recently bought a small shareholding in the Netherlands-based Independent Media group, which publishes Russian editions of Cosmopolitan, Harper's Bazaar, Good Housekeeping and Playboy.
Russia's biggest oil company, NK LUKoil, has recently bought a stake in the Moscow daily Izvestia.
